text: Pollution doesn't stop at the source.
It moves with the wind, crosses communities,
and puts vulnerable populations at risk.
But detecting an environmental threat is only the beginning.
The real challenge is knowing where it could go,
who could be affected, and what to do next.
Meet AERIS.
AERIS, the AI environmental risk and intervention system,
transforms environmental intelligence into actionable decisions.
It brings together fire detections,
air quality observations, weather conditions,
and the locations of critical public facilities.
Instead of looking at these signals in isolation,
AERIS connects them through a unified geospatial risk analysis pipeline.
The result is a clearer picture of an evolving environmental threat.
It begins with real-world data.
Satellite-based fire detections help identify potential pollution sources.
Air quality observations provide additional environmental context,
while weather and wind data help assess how conditions
may influence the movement of risk.
AERIS brings these signals together on a shared map,
helping decision makers understand not just what is happening,
but where it matters.
Every source contributes a different piece of the picture.
Next, AERIS examines the geography of potential impact.
Using source locations, wind conditions, and spatial analysis,
it identifies a potential risk corridor for further assessment.
This corridor helps narrow attention
to the areas that may require closer monitoring.
It is a decision support estimate,
not a guarantee of exactly where pollution will travel.
By making the potential impact area visible,
AERIS gives response teams a more focused starting point.
But a risk map alone is not enough.
Decision makers need to understand who could be affected.
AERIS combines geospatial analysis with population data
and nearby facility locations to estimate potential exposure.
In this scenario, the system ranks 444 sites
for further assessment and presents an estimated exposure range
of approximately 7.1 to 14.5 million people.
This range communicates uncertainty in the assessment.
It is not a statistical confidence interval
or account of confirmed exposures.
AERIS then turns analysis into priorities.
Schools, hospitals, and other relevant facilities
can be assessed according to their location
and potential exposure.
Instead of forcing teams to interpret disconnected data sets,
the system organizes the results into a ranked list.
This helps response teams identify which locations
may deserve attention first,
investigate the evidence behind each priority,
and focus limited resources where they may be needed most.
The final step is action.
AERIS presents a structured protection and response checklist,
helping teams move from identifying a threat
to evaluating appropriate protective measures.
The objective is simple.
Reduce the time spent piecing together information
and make the next decision clearer.
AERIS supports human decision makers.
Real-world interventions still depend on verification,
local conditions, and authorized response teams.
Behind this workflow is a modular data pipeline
connecting ingestion, validation, geospatial analysis,
exposure estimation, and action prioritization.
Each stage contributes to one continuous process,
turning environmental data
into decision-ready intelligence.
Environmental threats demand more than detection.
They demand informed decisions.
AERIS doesn't just help identify environmental risks,
it helps cities decide what to do next.
AERIS, from pollution source to protective action.
